facts.text: The masked lapwing is the largest member of its family, measuring 30 to 37 cm long with a wingspan of 75–85 cm.
facts.quote: The masked lapwing is the largest representative of the family Charadriidae. It measures from 30 to 37 cm (12 to 15 in) in length and has a wingspan of 75–85 cm (30–33 in)

facts.text: It calls at any time of day or night, with warning calls, defending calls, courtship calls and calls to its young.
facts.quote: The birds have a wide range of calls which can be heard at any time of the day or night: the warning call, a loud defending call, courtship calls, calls to its young, and others.

facts.text: Although it rests, the ground-dwelling lapwing never truly sleeps, staying alert at all times.
facts.quote: Since the bird lives on the ground, it is always alert and, even though it rests, it never sleeps properly.

facts.text: It nests on almost any open ground, including suburban parks, school ovals, supermarket carparks and flat rooftops.
facts.quote: being quite prepared to make a nest on almost any stretch of open ground, including suburban parks and gardens, school ovals, and even supermarket carparks and flat rooftops

facts.text: To lure predators away, a lapwing may fiercely guard a non-existent nest or hop on a single leg as a distraction.
facts.quote: The bird may also use diversion tactics against potential predators, such as fiercely protecting a non-existent nest, or a distraction display of hopping on a single leg

facts.text: Despite a widespread myth, the wing spur cannot inject venom.
facts.quote: There is a widely-believed myth that the spur can inject venom, however this is false.

facts.text: Young lapwings may stay with their parents for one to two years, forming family groups of three to five birds.
facts.quote: will often stay with the parents for from one to two years, resulting in family groups of three to five birds nesting in one location over the summer

facts.text: The masked lapwing spends most of its time on the ground searching for worms and insects to eat.
facts.quote: It spends most of its time on the ground searching for food such as insects and worms
